milestones.title: M0 — Foundation
milestones.description: Core implementation, artifact, evidence, and repository foundations.

milestones.title: M0.5 — Public project surface
milestones.description: Roadmap and agent foundation followed by the static website and generated status.

milestones.title: M1 — Validated MVP
milestones.description: One-phone Android, Linux guest, network, recovery, and durability path.

milestones.title: M2 — Early access
milestones.description: Release compliance, guided setup, verified downloads, and community testing.

milestones.title: M3 — Reliability
milestones.description: Thermal, storage, network, OEM lifecycle, upgrade, and device-class qualification.

milestones.title: M4 — Platform expansion
milestones.description: Isolation, authentication, reproducible builds, controller, hosts, profiles, and runtime adapters.

milestones.title: MVP+ — USB physical link
milestones.description: Android Open Accessory link, QEMU stream NIC, Linux TAP/NAT, fallback, and optional transfer.

labels.name: roadmap
labels.description: Normalized issue in the reviewed project roadmap.

labels.name: roadmap:public
labels.description: Summary may be published in the public roadmap.

labels.name: roadmap:internal
labels.description: Planning item is visible to maintainers but not public roadmap copy.

labels.name: agent:ready
labels.description: Dependency-clear packet reviewed for a future phase.

labels.name: agent:review
labels.description: Implementation or phase plan is under review.

labels.name: agent:hold
labels.description: Intentionally held for later phase review.

issues.title: Canonical profiles and artifact manifests
issues.publicSummary: Checked-in VM profiles and one strict artifact-manifest contract provide the production source of truth.
issues.observableOutcome: Profiles and manifests consumed by the app, tests, and laboratories are versioned, typed, and validated from one current representation.
nonGoals: Arbitrary ISO images or raw QEMU arguments.
validation: Profile and manifest checks pass.
No acceptance gate is inferred from issue state.
acceptanceCriteria: Canonical profile inputs are checked in.
Manifest consumers reject incomplete or executable fields.
Scope remains product-behaviour neutral.

issues.title: Authenticated resumable artifact upload
issues.publicSummary: A trusted controller can deliver large artifacts through bounded, authenticated, resumable, digest-verified upload.
issues.observableOutcome: The upload path resumes safely and publishes only a verified artifact manifest.
nonGoals: A production artifact update framework or delegated trust.
validation: Offline upload contract tests pass.
acceptanceCriteria: Upload is authenticated.
Digest verification precedes publication.
Resume and failure states are bounded.

issues.title: Evidence-bound HIL runner
issues.publicSummary: One physical-device runner records exact device, commit, and APK identity for hardware scenarios.
issues.observableOutcome: Physical scenarios use the configured serial and produce promotable evidence records without auto-selecting a device.
nonGoals: Using issue state or fake devices as physical evidence.
validation: HIL doctor and evidence checks pass when prerequisites exist.
acceptanceCriteria: The exact configured serial is required.
Evidence binds source and APK identity.
Secrets are redacted before publication.

issues.title: Deterministic Podroid provenance
issues.publicSummary: Podroid source, downstream patches, packaging hooks, and updates are deterministic and reviewable.
issues.observableOutcome: The pinned upstream source and project-owned changes can be reproduced and checked without silently accepting drift.
nonGoals: Replacing the APK-native QEMU path before physical evidence.
validation: Offline provenance and snapshot checks pass.
acceptanceCriteria: The upstream pin is explicit.
Downstream patches are ordered and reviewable.
Packaging checks use the pinned source identity.

issues.title: Phase and alpha compatibility guardrails
issues.publicSummary: Task tooling enforces one authorized phase and a clean-break unreleased-alpha compatibility policy.
issues.observableOutcome: Only the active DAG and reviewed packet authorize implementation, and obsolete development formats are not preserved by default.
nonGoals: Automatically activating queued tasks.
validation: Agent task and context checks pass.
acceptanceCriteria: The active DAG is explicit.
Packets define allowed paths.
Compatibility exceptions require named deployed populations and deletion triggers.

issues.title: Supervised device-lab safety
issues.publicSummary: Serial-specific leases, expiring authorization, evidence classes, and exact-input records make device work human-visible.
issues.observableOutcome: Diagnostic and candidate device runs have distinct authorization and promotion boundaries with reliable cleanup.
nonGoals: Treating a device lease as a production runtime requirement.
validation: Review the draft device-lab safety change.
Do not treat review state as acceptance evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: Authorization is serial-specific and expiring.
Evidence records preserve exact inputs.
Draft PR state remains visible.

issues.title: Accepted public-surface decisions
issues.publicSummary: Static-site, design-system, theme, roadmap-truth, Podroid alignment, and phase-replanning decisions are accepted.
issues.observableOutcome: The website and roadmap tooling have durable boundaries and separate authorities.
nonGoals: Adding website pages or product implementation.
validation: Accepted ADR and governance documents are reviewed.
acceptanceCriteria: Static publication is defined.
Roadmap, task, and acceptance authorities remain separate.
Theme and progressive-enhancement contracts are explicit.

issues.title: Issue roadmap and human-aware agent index
issues.publicSummary: GitHub issues and dependencies generate a bounded public roadmap, last-known-good snapshot, compact agent index, and per-issue context.
issues.observableOutcome: A complete normalized graph can be validated, synchronized, summarized, freshness-checked, and inspected in bounded context without silently granting work authorization.
nonGoals: Website pages, GitHub mutation during tests, and acceptance-gate changes.
validation: Seed, offline fixtures, focused tests, and repository checks pass.
Live dry-run remains a separately reported boundary.
acceptanceCriteria: The seed covers the reviewed roadmap.
Generation refuses partial graphs and stale fallback.
Context output is bounded and comment-free by default.

issues.title: Static website shell and theme
issues.publicSummary: Astro builds a component-based static shell with one token-driven CSS system and System/Light/Dark theme control.
issues.observableOutcome: The public shell remains useful without JavaScript and uses generated project data at build time.
nonGoals: Browser-side GitHub API calls.
validation: Static build, accessibility, and no-JavaScript checks pass.
acceptanceCriteria: Shared tokens and components are used.
System, Light, and Dark are visible and keyboard accessible.
The HTML baseline is complete without JavaScript.

issues.title: Public pages and honest copy
issues.publicSummary: Agreed user- and community-facing pages are published from shared components and evidence-aligned copy.
issues.observableOutcome: Each planned public page communicates current limits and does not invent validation claims.
nonGoals: A developer subsection or browser runtime dependency.
validation: Static HTML and link checks pass.
acceptanceCriteria: All agreed pages use shared components.
Copy distinguishes planned, implemented, and validated state.
No page hard-codes changing counts or device support.

issues.title: Generated status and evidence surface
issues.publicSummary: Acceptance, evidence, release, and roadmap data generate public status without hard-coded counts or candidate identities.
issues.observableOutcome: The site consumes reviewed generated data and preserves the distinction between issue completion and product validation.
nonGoals: Changing the acceptance ledger from a website build.
validation: Generated-data schema and stale-data checks pass.
acceptanceCriteria: Gate status comes from the ledger and evidence.
Candidate identity is generated, not hard-coded.
Stale data is visible or blocks publication as specified.

issues.title: Progressive roadmap and guide enhancements
issues.publicSummary: Roadmap filters, guide search, setup checklist, checksum verification, evidence drawers, and restrained motion progressively enhance static HTML.
issues.observableOutcome: Optional browser features improve navigation while the static baseline remains complete and accessible.
nonGoals: Client-side fetching of GitHub data.
validation: Keyboard, reduced-motion, and no-JavaScript checks pass.
acceptanceCriteria: Enhancements are component-scoped.
Reduced motion is respected.
Static HTML retains the same meaning.

issues.title: Exact static artifact deployment
issues.publicSummary: GitHub Actions validates and deploys the exact static artifact with source hashes and stale-data protection.
issues.observableOutcome: The deployed site is traceable to the validated source and generated inputs.
nonGoals: Publishing an unreviewed stale snapshot.
validation: CI artifact hash and deployment checks pass.
acceptanceCriteria: The exact validated artifact is deployed.
Source and data hashes are retained.
Stale-data protection fails closed for new deployment.

issues.title: Canonical Ubuntu guest boot qualification
issues.publicSummary: Ubuntu ARM64 UEFI boot, QMP, NoCloud, key-only loopback SSH, restart, and secret hygiene pass in one bounded host-QEMU run.
issues.observableOutcome: The canonical generic guest path is qualified without guest mesh or Android claims.
nonGoals: Closing physical Android gates or qualifying guest mesh.
validation: Run the bounded host-QEMU qualification.
Scan forbidden material and record exact profile/artifact identities.
acceptanceCriteria: Ubuntu UEFI reaches the expected boot state.
QMP and key-only loopback SSH work.
Restart and secret-hygiene checks pass.

issues.title: Guest mesh identity and recovery qualification
issues.publicSummary: One-use guest Headscale enrollment, separate identity, tailnet SSH, restart, interruption, and recovery are qualified without Android claims.
issues.observableOutcome: Guest mesh behavior is independently evidenced after canonical boot qualification.
nonGoals: Treating host-QEMU evidence as physical Android evidence.
validation: Use a disposable Headscale lab and bounded guest scenario.
acceptanceCriteria: Guest identity is separate from host identity.
One-use enrollment and SSH are verified.
Recovery remains available after mesh interruption.

issues.title: One-phone host runtime and mesh
issues.publicSummary: APK-native QEMU boots on one exact ARM64 Android phone and host Headscale/API reachability is established.
issues.observableOutcome: The product-critical phone path is evidenced with exact device and APK identity.
nonGoals: Emulator or host-QEMU substitution for physical evidence.
validation: Run the exact configured HIL smoke and host mesh/API scenarios.
acceptanceCriteria: APK-native QEMU boots on the configured phone.
Host mesh enrollment is evidenced.
Authenticated Host API is reachable through the host mesh.

issues.title: Controller-driven Ubuntu deployment
issues.publicSummary: The controller delivers Ubuntu artifacts, applies one generation, and reaches the separately enrolled guest with ordinary SSH.
issues.observableOutcome: Remote deployment works through typed host resources and guest SSH, with one active VM.
nonGoals: Moving orchestration state into the Android Host API.
validation: Run the bounded HIL MVP deployment scenario.
acceptanceCriteria: One generation is applied idempotently.
Guest enrollment is separate from host enrollment.
Ordinary SSH reaches the guest.

issues.title: Host-mediated recovery SSH
issues.publicSummary: Recovery SSH works through the host when guest mesh is unavailable.
issues.observableOutcome: A typed authenticated host tunnel keeps guest recovery available without an arbitrary shell endpoint.
nonGoals: Exposing raw QMP, raw shell, or host paths.
validation: Disable guest mesh in the HIL scenario and verify recovery.
acceptanceCriteria: The recovery route is authenticated.
Guest access works with mesh disabled.
No arbitrary host command surface is introduced.

issues.title: Lifecycle and outage resilience
issues.publicSummary: Activity, service, process, reboot-after-unlock, and controller/network outage reconcile without duplicate QEMU processes.
issues.observableOutcome: Desired state and operation journal survive the bounded lifecycle and controller-offline scenarios.
nonGoals: Claiming reliability across an untested OEM matrix.
validation: Run the resilience HIL scenario and inspect process uniqueness.
acceptanceCriteria: Graceful stop precedes force kill.
Designated data survives reset.
Reconciliation resumes after restart and controller outage.

issues.title: Base MVP evidence seal
issues.publicSummary: Every B01–B20 gate passes against one exact source commit, APK, device record, and reviewed evidence set.
issues.observableOutcome: The MVP claim is sealed only when all base evidence records satisfy their schemas and identity constraints.
nonGoals: Starting USB while any base gate is red.
validation: Run the phase-end evidence review against one exact candidate.
Do not infer a gate from issue closure.
acceptanceCriteria: All B01–B20 records are PASS.
Source and APK identity match across evidence.
Review confirms no physical claim was substituted by software checks.

issues.title: Release compliance review
issues.publicSummary: Licensing, notices, corresponding source, modification records, and exact binary/source relationship are reviewed before public APK distribution.
issues.observableOutcome: The repository has a documented compliance position for a public release.
nonGoals: Blocking private source development or local device-lab builds.
validation: Complete a reviewed licensing and source correspondence check.
acceptanceCriteria: Licenses and notices are published.
Modification records are present.
The release binary maps to exact source and inputs.

issues.title: Guided local setup
issues.publicSummary: A guided local setup explains trust, permissions, profiles, progress, recovery, and current limits.
issues.observableOutcome: A new maintainer or tester can follow setup without hidden credentials or unsupported claims.
nonGoals: Supporting unqualified device classes.
validation: Documentation review and link checks pass.
acceptanceCriteria: Trust and permission boundaries are explicit.
Recovery and current limits are documented.
Tested environment identities are named.

issues.title: First public device records
issues.publicSummary: First public device records bind model, Android version, build, profile, evidence, duration, thermal notes, and limitations.
issues.observableOutcome: Device support is described from exact reviewed records rather than generic compatibility claims.
nonGoals: Claiming broad Android support from one device.
validation: Review redacted device records and evidence links.
acceptanceCriteria: Each record names exact device facts.
Limitations and thermal notes are retained.
Public copy does not overgeneralize.

issues.title: Verified downloads
issues.publicSummary: Downloads publish an exact compliant APK, checksum, signing/source identity, and physical-validation status.
issues.observableOutcome: A download consumer can verify what binary was built and what it has or has not proved.
nonGoals: Publishing an APK before release compliance and MVP evidence.
validation: Checksum, signing, source, and status checks pass.
acceptanceCriteria: The exact artifact is downloadable.
Checksum and signing identity are shown.
Physical-validation status is truthful.

issues.title: Tested installation and recovery guides
issues.publicSummary: Installation, enrollment, deployment, SSH, recovery, reset, diagnostics, and removal guides identify tested builds and environments.
issues.observableOutcome: Operational guides stay coupled to tested contracts and explain safe failure handling.
nonGoals: Documenting unsupported arbitrary image workflows.
validation: Guide review uses exact tested build identities.
acceptanceCriteria: Each guide names its tested environment.
Recovery and removal are explicit.
Credentials are not embedded in examples.

issues.title: Community test-day kit
issues.publicSummary: A safe community test-day kit covers consent, battery checks, setup, evidence, redaction, and follow-up.
issues.observableOutcome: Community testing has a supervised, privacy-aware procedure with bounded evidence collection.
nonGoals: Unsupervised destructive device automation.
validation: Human review of consent, cleanup, and redaction steps.
acceptanceCriteria: Consent and stop conditions are visible.
Evidence is redacted and bounded.
Follow-up and cleanup are documented.

issues.title: Diagnostics and support UX
issues.publicSummary: Diagnostics and support UX explain operation state and recovery without exposing credentials or guest data.
issues.observableOutcome: Users can understand bounded failures and collect safe diagnostic material.
nonGoals: Adding a general debug shell or raw QMP endpoint.
validation: Redaction and support-flow tests pass.
acceptanceCriteria: Operation state is legible.
Recovery guidance is bounded.
Credentials and guest data remain excluded.

issues.title: Sustained workload qualification
issues.publicSummary: Sustained workload classes have duration, charging, temperature, throttling, and stop-policy evidence.
issues.observableOutcome: Resource and thermal behavior is measured for stated workload classes.
nonGoals: Generalizing results beyond measured workload classes.
validation: Run bounded duration and thermal scenarios.
acceptanceCriteria: Duration and charging conditions are recorded.
Thermal and throttling observations are recorded.
Stop policy is explicit.

issues.title: Storage pressure and reset qualification
issues.publicSummary: Storage pressure, data export, reset, and uninstall behavior are bounded and documented.
issues.observableOutcome: Data-preservation and cleanup behavior is measured under constrained storage.
nonGoals: Supporting unbounded storage growth.
validation: Run storage-pressure and reset scenarios with evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: Data export is bounded.
Reset and uninstall semantics are documented.
Pressure failure is safe and observable.

issues.title: Network interruption qualification
issues.publicSummary: Host and guest behavior across network changes, relay paths, and Headscale interruption is qualified.
issues.observableOutcome: Mesh and recovery behavior under stated network failures is measured.
nonGoals: Adding a second mesh provider in this outcome.
validation: Run bounded network interruption scenarios.
acceptanceCriteria: Network transitions are observed.
Recovery remains available.
Relay and Headscale interruption limits are recorded.

issues.title: Android lifecycle matrix
issues.publicSummary: Selected Android versions and OEMs have comparable lifecycle evidence.
issues.observableOutcome: Supported device classes are based on comparable lifecycle scenarios.
nonGoals: Claiming every Android OEM is supported.
validation: Run the same bounded lifecycle suite on selected devices.
acceptanceCriteria: Device facts are recorded.
Lifecycle results are comparable.
Unsupported combinations remain explicit.

issues.title: Measured resource admission
issues.publicSummary: Measured memory, storage, battery, and thermal facts drive resource admission and device classes.
issues.observableOutcome: Admission decisions use recorded device facts rather than broad assumptions.
nonGoals: Multiple active VMs in the MVP.
validation: Test admission against measured device classes.
acceptanceCriteria: Resource thresholds are typed.
Admission is observable.
Thermal and storage limits are enforced safely.

issues.title: Upgrade and rollback continuity
issues.publicSummary: App upgrade, rollback, and runtime continuity have a documented tested path.
issues.observableOutcome: Desired state and designated data remain understandable across the supported upgrade path.
nonGoals: A production update framework.
validation: Run upgrade and rollback scenarios on selected devices.
acceptanceCriteria: Supported upgrade path is named.
Rollback behavior is recorded.
Runtime continuity and data boundaries are verified.

issues.title: QEMU isolation and image threat model
issues.publicSummary: QEMU is isolated from controller credentials through a proven boundary and arbitrary-image risk is modeled.
issues.observableOutcome: The project can state which image classes are safe for the selected isolation boundary.
nonGoals: Promising arbitrary hostile images before isolation is proven.
validation: Review the threat model and boundary evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: Credential separation is evidenced.
Image classes and risks are explicit.
Raw host paths and arguments remain unavailable.

issues.title: Project-owned native reproducibility
issues.publicSummary: QEMU, launcher, libslirp, kernel, initramfs, and profile artifacts are built from pinned project-owned sources.
issues.observableOutcome: Native runtime inputs have reproducible provenance beyond extracted upstream release assets.
nonGoals: Changing the current packaging path before the replacement is qualified.
validation: Reproduce native artifacts from pinned source.
acceptanceCriteria: Sources and patches are pinned.
Artifact provenance is recorded.
The built inputs match the packaged contract.

issues.title: Rust and Slint controller
issues.publicSummary: A Rust controller core and Slint desktop application replace the Python test client without changing host contracts.
issues.observableOutcome: A cross-platform controller implementation reuses the stable typed Host API.
nonGoals: Moving domain contracts into a UI toolkit.
validation: Controller contract and cross-platform tests pass.
acceptanceCriteria: Host API resource shapes remain stable.
Controller core is platform-independent.
Native tools stay outside browser runtime concerns.

issues.title: Rust host service
issues.publicSummary: Linux, SBC, and WSL hosts implement the same host API and operation semantics through a Rust service.
issues.observableOutcome: The host boundary is reusable outside Android while preserving typed lifecycle semantics.
nonGoals: Adding orchestrator state to the Host API.
validation: Cross-host contract and lifecycle tests pass.
acceptanceCriteria: Host resources match the typed contract.
Operation semantics are durable.
Platform adapters remain replaceable.

issues.title: Additional ARM64 profiles and K3s worker
issues.publicSummary: Additional ARM64 profiles satisfy the guest contract and a real K3s worker joins, drains, leaves, and recovers under an external control plane.
issues.observableOutcome: A second concrete guest family and real worker lifecycle prove the profile boundary beyond the MVP.
nonGoals: Moving Kubernetes orchestration into the Android application.
validation: Profile and external-control-plane qualification passes.
acceptanceCriteria: Guest-class contract is reused.
A real worker lifecycle is evidenced.
Drain, leave, and recovery are recorded.

issues.title: Second mesh provider
issues.publicSummary: Nebula or another structurally different mesh adapter validates the host-mesh port.
issues.observableOutcome: A second provider proves the host mesh boundary is not coupled to one implementation.
nonGoals: Changing the MVP host mesh before physical evidence.
validation: Adapter contract and interruption tests pass.
acceptanceCriteria: Provider-specific code is behind the host-mesh port.
Identity boundaries remain separate.
Failure and recovery are compared.

issues.title: Signed artifact distribution
issues.publicSummary: TUF metadata and digest-addressed OCI/ORAS transport protect normalized bootable artifact distribution.
issues.observableOutcome: Artifact publication and retrieval have reviewed metadata and digest integrity.
nonGoals: Adding a production update framework to the MVP.
validation: Verify signed metadata, digests, and rollback handling.
acceptanceCriteria: Metadata is signed and verified.
Artifacts are addressed by digest.
Rollback and delegation boundaries are documented.

issues.title: Multiple VM isolation
issues.publicSummary: Multiple VM instances have isolated paths, identities, disks, operations, and measured admission.
issues.observableOutcome: The one-VM MVP limit can be lifted only with explicit per-instance isolation and resource accounting.
nonGoals: Multiple active VMs in the base MVP.
validation: Isolation, admission, and lifecycle tests pass.
acceptanceCriteria: Instance paths and identities are isolated.
Operations are independently durable.
Admission is measured.

issues.title: Principal authorization and revocation
issues.publicSummary: The capability adapter is replaced by reviewed mTLS/principal authorization with bounded multi-controller recovery and revocation.
issues.observableOutcome: Controller identity and revocation are explicit without changing bounded Host API resources.
nonGoals: A general remote shell or unbounded credential delegation.
validation: Principal, recovery, and revocation tests pass.
acceptanceCriteria: Principals are authenticated.
Revocation is observable and bounded.
Recovery does not broaden command authority.

issues.title: Docker and Swarm reference provisioning
issues.publicSummary: Docker and Swarm reference provisioning joins, drains, leaves, replaces, and recovers a phone worker without moving orchestrator state into the Host API.
issues.observableOutcome: A reference workload integration uses the existing host boundary and keeps orchestration external.
nonGoals: Kubernetes, Swarm, or Nomad orchestration inside Android.
validation: External control-plane lifecycle evidence passes.
acceptanceCriteria: Join, drain, leave, replace, and recovery are tested.
Orchestrator state remains external.
Host API remains typed and bounded.

issues.title: Managed Android reliability tiers
issues.publicSummary: Device Owner and narrowly patched Android deployments provide explicit managed reliability tiers without a general root shell.
issues.observableOutcome: Managed deployment options are described as separate tiers with explicit security and lifecycle boundaries.
nonGoals: Adding a general root shell.
validation: Managed-device security and lifecycle review passes.
acceptanceCriteria: Reliability tiers are explicit.
Permissions and threat boundaries are documented.
No general root endpoint is added.

issues.title: AVF runtime adapter
issues.publicSummary: AVF is implemented behind the same runtime contract and compared with QEMU on supported devices.
issues.observableOutcome: A second runtime can be evaluated without coupling permanent contracts to one engine.
nonGoals: Replacing QEMU before physical evidence proves a better backend.
validation: Runtime contract and comparative device evidence pass.
acceptanceCriteria: AVF is behind the runtime port.
Comparison uses the same workload contract.
QEMU remains available as the known-good path.

issues.title: Delegated profile repository
issues.publicSummary: A remote profile repository supports signed publication, controlled delegation, and reviewed profile-maintainer boundaries.
issues.observableOutcome: Profile updates have an explicit trust and review chain without weakening local validation.
nonGoals: Unreviewed remote executable configuration.
validation: Delegation, signature, and rejection tests pass.
acceptanceCriteria: Publication is signed.
Delegation is bounded.
Local typed validation remains authoritative before use.

issues.title: Local controller browser bridge
issues.publicSummary: A browser interface works through a local controller bridge that keeps keys, SSH, tunnels, and native tools outside the browser.
issues.observableOutcome: Browser convenience does not turn the public site into a credential or arbitrary-command surface.
nonGoals: Browser-native private keys or host shell access.
validation: Bridge authorization and browser security checks pass.
acceptanceCriteria: Keys remain outside browser storage.
Bridge operations are typed.
The public website remains static.

issues.title: Guest class and image-source separation
issues.publicSummary: Guest class, immutable image identity, source provider, and distro bootstrap adapter are separated and proved by concrete families.
issues.observableOutcome: The profile boundary can grow beyond the MVP without exposing raw QEMU or host configuration.
nonGoals: Arbitrary image support before QEMU isolation.
validation: Concrete profile families pass the typed contract.
acceptanceCriteria: Class and immutable identity are distinct.
Source providers are bounded.
No raw runtime or host fields are exposed.

issues.title: Android Open Accessory control link
issues.publicSummary: Linux and Android establish a bounded, reconnectable Android Open Accessory control link.
issues.observableOutcome: A supervised USB control channel is established with explicit reconnect and cleanup semantics.
nonGoals: Starting USB before every base gate passes.
validation: Run the physical USB scenario after RELEASE-01.
acceptanceCriteria: AOA link is bounded.
Reconnect and cleanup are reliable.
Base MVP gate remains a prerequisite.

issues.title: QEMU USB stream NIC
issues.publicSummary: The guest receives a second QEMU NIC over the Android USB stream bridge while SLIRP remains available.
issues.observableOutcome: USB networking adds a bounded secondary path without removing recovery fallback.
nonGoals: Replacing SLIRP as the fallback path.
validation: Run the authorized USB physical scenario.
acceptanceCriteria: The second NIC is bounded.
SLIRP remains available.
Disconnect does not remove recovery.

issues.title: Linux TAP and NAT bridge
issues.publicSummary: node-linkd provides bounded Linux TAP/NAT connectivity and reports link health.
issues.observableOutcome: The Linux side of the USB data path has explicit ownership and health reporting.
nonGoals: Unbounded host network reconfiguration.
validation: Run TAP/NAT and link-health checks in the authorized lab.
acceptanceCriteria: TAP/NAT is bounded.
Link health is observable.
Cleanup restores the host path.

issues.title: USB routing fallback
issues.publicSummary: Guest routing prefers healthy USB and returns to SLIRP after disconnect without losing recovery.
issues.observableOutcome: USB interruption preserves the already-qualified fallback and recovery route.
nonGoals: Using USB to close base-MVP gates.
validation: Disconnect and reconnect the physical USB path.
acceptanceCriteria: Healthy USB is preferred.
SLIRP resumes after disconnect.
Recovery remains available throughout.

issues.title: Hardened USB protocol
issues.publicSummary: The USB protocol supports optional bounded artifact transfer, version negotiation, diagnostics, and hardening without weakening fallback.
issues.observableOutcome: The post-MVP USB protocol has a reviewed extension surface and safe failure behavior.
nonGoals: Making optional artifact transfer a base-MVP requirement.
validation: Protocol version, diagnostics, and hardening review pass.
acceptanceCriteria: Version negotiation is bounded.
Optional transfer is digest-verified.
Fallback and recovery are not weakened.

releaseBlockingDebt.summary: Canonical Ubuntu guest boot is not qualified end to end.
Repository-wide release compliance is not documented.
Native Podroid runtime assets are extracted from a pinned upstream APK.
The node-shell module owns too many production responsibilities.
The Tailscale adapter mixes runtime, LocalAPI, VPN, platform, and persistence concerns.
Enrollment is two bound imports rather than one user-facing bundle.
The controller remains a Python MVP CLI.
USB/AOA remains blocked until every base gate passes.

postMvpDirections.summary: Strong QEMU isolation and arbitrary-image threat model.
Additional Linux profiles and real K3s worker.
Device Owner and patched Android tiers.
Rust/Slint controller and Linux/SBC/WSL host service.
Remote profile repository and delegated maintainers.
Web UI through a local controller bridge.

pullRequests.title: Podroid-MVP alignment and public roadmap governance
